Financial research AI just beat Claude on benchmark testing while running at 11x lower cost per query.

Domain-specific post-training is rapidly shifting the economics of enterprise AI deployment. We are seeing specialized smaller models outpace massive foundation models in dedicated fields.

Here are the key technical developments from across the industry today:

🤖 Samaya AI released Sterling, a 3B-active parameter model for financial research built on Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Sterling achieved a 58.9% score on the FrontierFinance benchmark at $0.61 per question, compared to Claude Fable 5.1 scoring 55.9% at $6.89 per question.

🚨 Anthropic reported a supply chain security incident involving its verified Cursor extension for VS Code, which was backdoored for nearly 12 hours. Investigation is ongoing into how attackers obtained access to the verified account.

🛡️ AI-driven code audit tools are standardizing their detection mechanisms. Anthropic, OpenAI, Cloudflare, and Google all released AI security agents that scan source code using a shared control loop: find the bug, attempt to disprove it, and generate a patch.

🌐 Big tech providers agreed on a unified web scraping control for content creators. OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic are adopting a shared policy token standard, allowing publishers to set AI training opt-out preferences across multiple platforms simultaneously.

The shift toward domain-tailored smaller models and automated code security agents highlights where engineering effort is concentrating right now.
